quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: You must yield to emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you a roundabout is coming. Enter slowly and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When parallel parking, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Stop next to the car in front of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop parallel to the car in front of your space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for other traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic will merge into your lane from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic will merge into your lane from the right.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic from the right will merge into your lane. Be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you will turn.

questions.question: You wait to turn left at a wide intersection. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for a driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and the turn is safe.

questions.question: Should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: Yes, if the car ahead is turning left.
Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull off the road.

questions.question: You drive up a hill toward a heavy truck. You should know:

options.text: The truck may go slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large trucks go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. It is unsafe and illegal to pass on a hill with poor visibility.

questions.question: A traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass before it turns red.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may only proceed if there is also a circular green light.
It shows the direction to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, just like a green light. However, you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, when exiting a highway, when following a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a rural highway if no other limit is posted?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a rural highway is 75 mph. Always follow posted speed limit signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: You are driving slowly and cars are backing up behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, pull off to the right and let them pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle can cross them to pass in either direction.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right edge and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren on an emergency vehicle, pull to the right edge of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: When is the road most slippery?

options.text: After one to two hours of rain.

questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water and create a slick surface.

questions.question: A child on a bicycle is riding near your vehicle. What should you expect?

options.text: The child has full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. They may change direction suddenly without warning. Children and bicycles are small and easy to miss, so be extra careful.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Usually slows down the driver's reaction to hazards.
Usually makes the driver go faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows down the driver's reaction to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially when turning. Slow down for turns and curves in slippery conditions.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says not to. When turning, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for trains from both directions.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with care. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, like school buses and hazardous material trucks.
